name: rustic cobbled work yard ground autotile: rounded warm river cobbles with dark earth joints, a low dressed stone kerb rim with a 2px front face on the south edge, grass tufts at the rim, lying flat on grass (top-down 3/4 RPG ground)
label: beodeul_yard/cobble

surfaces.part: cobbled ground field (warm cobbles with dark joints)
dressed stone kerb rim with a 2px south face

answer.evidence: This is a flat terrain autotile patch seen from above. The cobble field is a very large top-down surface with a hole where grass shows through. The light stone kerb runs around the edge, and its south-facing edges have only about 2 rows of front face plus a thin shadow. That is under the 3-row minimum for a front face, so the patch reads as a top-down slab, not a three-quarter block. It has no side face and no standing volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 18 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the reference grass and 7 for the reference paving. Near-flat coverage is only 3%, so there are no real flat fills. The cobbles are shaded one by one, with warm and grey stones each carrying about 4-5 lightness steps and a highlight dot, set in dark brown earth joints. The 0% neutral share of dark edge pixels means the outlines and joints lean brown rather than black, so they read as dark material tone and not a sticker line. The pale dressed-stone kerb has a visible lit top and a darker south front face, and grass tufts sit at the rim. The surrounding grass is subtler than the reference grass but still carries variation. The cobble pattern is somewhat repetitive, but it holds up at the reference's scale and detail level.

surfaces.part: cobble ground field (river cobbles with dark joints)
dressed stone kerb rim, south front face

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile that covers the whole 176x144 sheet. The cobble field is a large top-down surface of roughly 136 rows of cobbles with dark joints. The only vertical element is a light stone kerb with a 2-row front face on the south edges, for example the light rows just under the dark cobble rows in the lower part of the column scans. That is under the 3-row minimum for a front face. There is no eave shadow, no ellipse and no receding side face. The grass hole in the middle and the grass tufts are flat ground detail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 18 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 3%, so the cobble field has almost no flat blocks. Each cobble is shaded individually with a highlight, a mid tone and a shadow, in both warm and grey variants, and sits in dark earth joints. The kerb rim reads as stone with light, mid and dark steps and a visible south face. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean brown or earthy rather than black. This matches the Beodeul habit of using the adjacent material's dark tone. Weaknesses: the cobble pattern repeats fairly uniformly, and the surrounding grass looks quieter than the grass reference. Neither is enough to drop it below the references on density or texture.

surfaces.part: cobblestone yard field (rounded cobbles with dark earth joints)
dressed stone kerb rim, south front face
grass tufts at the rim and surrounding grass

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile patch (irregular cobble area with a grass hole), not a standing object. The cobble field is a large top-down surface seen from above, with warm and grey cobbles separated by dark joints. The only vertical element is the pale stone kerb, a thin rim around the patch. Its south-edge front face is about 2 rows, below the 3-row minimum for a front face. No receding side face is drawn, and the kerb is a rim rather than a separate volume. By the measurement rules this is a flat top-down slab, which is expected for ground terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 18 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 3%, close to the references' 0%. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the joints and rim lines lean brown rather than black, which fits dark_material_tone. The cobbles are rounded and shaded one by one in warm brown, tan and grey, with 4-5 lightness steps each and dark earth joints between them. The kerb has a lighter top face and a darker 2px south face. Grass tufts sit along the rim. Nothing is a flat fill. The cobble pattern is fairly uniform and repetitive, but it carries as much information as the references and more than the grass.

surfaces.part: dressed stone kerb rim with 2px south front face (light stone edge line plus dark joint)

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile. The cobble field is a large top-down surface of rounded stones and dark joints, about 130 rows tall. Its only vertical face is the thin light-stone kerb on the south edges, which the scan shows as about 2 rows (for example x=44 around rows 45-46, x=131 around rows 35-36). That is under the 3-row minimum for a front face. There is no ellipse, roof or open container, and no receding side face is drawn. The kerb rim reads as a rim or lip, not as a wall face, so the tile reads as a flat top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 18 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, so it is at or above both on density. Near-flat coverage is only 3%, so there are no large flat fills. The cobbles are shaded one by one in several warm and grey steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, and a dark earth joint), which is close to the 5-6 steps of the references. The 0% neutral share of dark edge pixels means the outlines and joints lean brown, matching dark_material_tone rather than a black sticker line. The stone kerb has a light top face and a darker 2px front face on the south edge, and the grass around it has some tuft texture. The grass outside the patch looks a little flatter and more repetitive than the reference grass, but this is minor. A careful artist would accept the piece next to the references.
